summary: Full backend + frontend regression for the NEW multi-manager (recipients) feature. Backend: 25/25 pytest cases pass sequentially (13 existing regression + 5 new-features + 7 recipients). Recipients CRUD, code regeneration + unpair, /pairing/claim wrong-code 400, device-single-manager move, /pairing/whoami paired+assigned semantics, PUT /schedule/assign (set/clear/404), and ALARMS GATING all verified: assigned manager device gets due alarms, other paired manager gets 0, unpaired desktop (device_id not registered) still gets due alarms as a fail-safe, no device_id also gets alarms as fail-safe, and clearing assignment zeros paired-manager alarms. Regression: manual anchor timing (shed 7:00 -> auger 01:00, 5:00 catch -> 23:00 prev-day auger), /schedule/delay +120 shifts and does not compound, my_farms limits arming, /recipients app_url payload builds https web /pair?code=NNN + qr_data_url. Frontend @1360 dashboard: crew-panel + assign-<id> + qr-<id> + regen-manager + remove-<id> + add-manager-input/button all working; header pill updates to 'On catch: TEST_UI' after assign toggle; QR/code visible in manager-qr; remove works and unassigns. Frontend @390 mobile settings: pairing-card renders unpaired form with pairing-code-input + pair-button; NO settings-qr and NO unpair-button (as required); entering Sam's code + pair-button shows 'Paired as Sam' with Off pill (Dave on catch) and 'Switch manager' UI. Frontend @390 mobile home: paired-chip reflects whoami ('Paired: Sam' when paired-but-not-assigned; 'Not paired' when fresh device). Frontend auto-pair /pair?code=<manager code>: pair-status flips to 'Paired! Opening your schedule…' then router.replace to /(tabs)/home and paired-chip shows 'Paired: Sam'. Bug found & fixed: getDeviceId() had a race across concurrent callers (AlarmOverlay + Settings/Home each called it on mount, both generated a fresh uuid, only the last write to AsyncStorage won — so useQuery(whoami) used a different device_id than pairing/claim's device_id, breaking paired-as/paired-chip on first load after clean storage). Root cause: /app/frontend/src/utils/device.ts had no in-flight cache. Fix: added module-level Promise cache so concurrent callers share the same id. Verified after restart: 'Paired as Sam' now appears on settings and 'Paired: Sam' on home reliably.

getDeviceId race condition was fixed in /app/frontend/src/utils/device.ts by caching the in-flight promise. Please review the fix and keep it — it prevents divergent device ids between concurrent callers (whoami vs claim vs alarms/active). Without this, a fresh phone loading Settings would sometimes fail to show 'Paired as X' after a successful pair.
critical_code_review_comments: settings.tsx invalidates qk.whoami but the useQuery key is [...qk.whoami, deviceId] — fine, prefix-match works, but consider consolidating deviceId provisioning into a single useDeviceId() hook to remove the get/set duplication across settings, home, pair and AlarmOverlay.

pair.tsx does router.replace to (tabs)/home after 1.2s but the whoami query on home uses refetchInterval, so the first render can flash 'Not paired' before flipping to 'Paired: <name>'. Consider awaiting qc.refetchQueries({ queryKey: qk.whoami }) before navigating.
alarms/active fail-safe: unregistered device_id and missing device_id both return due alarms. This is correct per spec but worth calling out in a comment near the endpoint to prevent regressions.

AlarmOverlay is global and pops over the dashboard whenever any pending alarm is past due; keep clicking alarm-done-button in playbooks before asserting non-overlay UI. Behaviour verified as designed.

rca_of_issue: Symptom: after entering a valid pairing code on mobile Settings, `paired-as` never appeared and Home's `paired-chip` sometimes showed 'Not paired' even though POST /api/pairing/claim returned 200. Reproduction: clear localStorage, load /(tabs)/settings, enter a manager code, tap Pair. Root cause: /app/frontend/src/utils/device.ts::getDeviceId did storage.getItem() and, if missing, generated a fresh uuid and called storage.setItem(); AlarmOverlay, Settings whoami effect, and the claim mutation each called getDeviceId concurrently on cold storage, generating 2-3 different ids in parallel; last-write-wins in AsyncStorage, so one component (claim) posted device_id A while another (whoami useQuery) polled device_id B — the backend correctly returned paired:false for the losing id. Fix: cache the in-flight Promise at module scope so all concurrent callers await and receive the same id; subsequent calls short-circuit via the cached promise. Re-tested end-to-end: settings shows 'Paired as Sam', home shows 'Paired: Sam', auto-pair /pair?code redirects and home reflects the pair.
